name: Chicken
notes__en:
The Chicken is the first pet almost everyone hatches. Its egg sits in the Forest right next to your base, needs no Speed to reach, and hatches faster than any other egg in our list, so a new player can have one earning within a minute of joining.

That is where the good news ends: the Chicken has the lowest base income of every pet we track. Treat it as a stepping stone. Two or three Chickens pay for nothing on their own, but the Speed you pick up while grabbing their eggs adds up, and that is what opens the rest of the Forest.

We used a Golden Chicken for our first in-game test of the income formula, and the result matched the calculator. If you hatch a heavy or mutated Chicken it is still worth keeping for a short while, but swap it out as soon as you can carry Raccoon or Fox eggs home.
source_note: Base income and weight from the wiki pet data module

name: Dog
notes__en:
The Dog is the second Common in the Forest and earns twice what a Chicken does. Its egg takes a little longer to hatch, but both are quick enough that the difference does not matter much.

One thing that confuses players: the Dog's base weight is roughly three times the Chicken's. A Dog card that shows a big number in kg is often just an average Dog, so do not get excited by the weight alone. Income only goes up when a pet is heavy compared with its own base weight, which is exactly what the weight table on this page shows.

In practice the Dog is a filler pet for your first few minutes. If your pen is full, a Dog is one of the first things to replace, and a Frog or Duckling from the Lake already beats it once you have the Speed to get there.
source_note: Base income and weight from the wiki pet data module

name: Bird
source_note: Base income and weight from the wiki pet data module

name: Burrowing Owl
notes__en:
The Burrowing Owl is the first Rare most players reach, because its egg spawns in the Forest. It earns many times what any Forest Common does, so hatching one is a real jump in income for a new base.

Its base weight is very low, the same as a Chicken's. That matters more than it looks: weight is compared with the pet's own base, so even a small Burrowing Owl can count as heavy and earn well above its base income. Owls are one of the best pets to roll for weight early in the game.

The Owl's main rival is the Raccoon from the same biome, which earns a bit more per second. If you have room for only one Rare from the Forest, take whichever came out heavier or with a mutation, because those two factors outweigh the small gap in base income.
source_note: Base income and weight from the wiki pet data module

name: Raccoon
notes__en:
The Raccoon is the strongest Rare in the Forest. It earns a little more than the Burrowing Owl and hatches a little slower, so it is the natural target once your first few pets are running.

Raccoon eggs are close to your base, which makes them a safe pick when the Lake still feels risky. Bringing back a few of them is often the quickest way to build enough Cash and Speed for the next step.

Its base weight is about twice the Owl's, so a Raccoon needs to roll heavier to get the same weight bonus. If you hatch a Golden or Rainbow Raccoon, keep it: a mutated Raccoon can carry an early base until you reach the Epics. Otherwise, plan to replace it with a Fox or Bear from the same biome.
source_note: Base income and weight from the wiki pet data module

name: Fox
notes__en:
The Fox is the first Epic in the game and the best value pet in the Forest for most players. It earns several times what the Raccoon does and its egg is still close to your base.

The Fox egg takes noticeably longer to hatch than any Forest Rare, so put it in your pen when you are about to spend a few minutes running elsewhere. A light base weight means a heavy Fox gets a good income boost from its weight.

A Golden or Rainbow Fox is one of the strongest pets a new player can realistically own. If you are choosing between a Fox and a Bear, the Bear earns a bit more, but the Fox hatches faster and gains more from a good weight roll.
source_note: Base income and weight from the wiki pet data module

name: Bear
notes__en:
The Bear is the Forest's top Epic. It earns a third more than the Fox and its egg hatches slower, so it is a good pet to work toward before you leave the Forest for good.

Its base weight is many times the Fox's, so big kg numbers on a Bear card are normal rather than special, and its weight bonus is smaller than a Fox's.

The Bear is a strong anchor for an early base, but it is quickly beaten once you can reach the Lake's Swan or the Snow biome's Walrus. Keep a mutated Bear for longer; replace a plain one as soon as your Speed allows.
source_note: Base income and weight from the wiki pet data module

name: Brr Brr Patapim
notes__en:
Brr Brr Patapim is the Forest's Legendary, named after a popular internet meme character. It is the best pet you can hatch without leaving the first biome.

Its egg takes minutes to hatch, the longest wait in the Forest. Its base weight is large, which means big kg numbers on its card are normal.

Compared with the Lake's Axolotl, Brr Brr Patapim earns less, so it is a starter Legendary rather than a long-term one. It is still a good target for a new player who cannot reach the Lake yet.
source_note: Base income and weight from the wiki pet data module

name: Frog
notes__en:
The Frog is the cheapest egg in the Lake, the second biome, and it shows why moving on from the Forest matters. A Frog earns more than a Forest Dog, and the Speed reward listed for its egg is about twice what the Forest's Legendary egg gives.

That makes Frog eggs a good Speed farm right after you unlock the Lake. They hatch quickly, they are light to carry, and the guardian is less of a problem when you only run to the nearest nests.

The Frog's base weight is tiny, so even a small-looking Frog can be heavy compared with its base and earn noticeably more. Check the weight on the card before you sell or replace one. As a long-term pet it does not last; Turtles and Swans from the same biome are far better once you can reach their nests safely.
source_note: Base income and weight from the wiki pet data module

name: Duckling
notes__en:
The Duckling is the best Common pet you can get before the Desert. It sits one step above the Frog in the Lake, earns a little more, and takes only a few seconds longer to hatch.

Like the Frog, it has a very light base weight, which means weight rolls change its income a lot. A Duckling that hatches a few times heavier than its base can earn as much as a plain Uncommon, which is a nice surprise early on.

The Speed reward on the Duckling egg is also a step up from the Frog's. If you are trying to save up Speed for the Desert, alternating Frog and Duckling eggs in the Lake is a steady way to do it without risking the slower, heavier eggs near the guardian.

name: Turtle
notes__en:
The Turtle is the Lake's Rare and earns more than either Forest Rare. It is the pet that makes the Lake worth farming for income, not just for Speed.

The Turtle's base weight is much higher than the Owl's or Raccoon's, so heavy-looking Turtles are common and usually only average. Do not keep a Turtle over a better pet just because the kg number is big; check the weight table on this page to see how much a heavier one really adds.

Its egg hatches at the same pace as the Raccoon's, and its Speed reward is several times larger. If you are deciding between running for Forest Rares or Lake Rares, the Lake wins on both counts once you have the Speed to get there and back.

name: Swan
notes__en:
The Swan is the Lake's Epic and the strongest Epic you can reach before the Desert. It earns more than either Forest Epic and is also the Lake's guardian, so its nests are where the danger is.

That makes Swan eggs a test of your Speed: you need to get close to the guardian and run back with the egg. Its light base weight is a bonus once you get one home, because a heavy Swan gains a lot from its weight.

A heavy or mutated Swan is a great early-to-mid game pet. Most players keep one until they reach Legendaries such as the Axolotl from the same biome.
source_note: Base income and weight from the wiki pet data module

name: Axolotl
notes__en:
The Axolotl is the Lake's Legendary, and it is the best pet most players can get from the first two biomes. It earns well over half again as much as the Forest's Legendary, Brr Brr Patapim.

The catch is the hatch time: Legendary eggs take minutes, not seconds. Put an Axolotl egg in your pen before you leave to farm elsewhere, so the wait does not feel slow.

Its base weight is light, so a heavy Axolotl gets a big weight boost. A Golden or Rainbow Axolotl is a top early pet that stays useful well into the Desert and Jungle.
source_note: Base income and weight from the wiki pet data module

name: Leviathan
notes__en:
The Leviathan is the surprise of the Lake: a Cosmic pet in the second biome. It earns far more than anything else you can reach at that stage, including the Axolotl.

The price is time. Its egg takes close to half an hour to hatch, much longer than any other Lake egg, so start it before a long farming session.

Its base weight is very heavy, so huge kg numbers are normal and weight bonuses are small. For a player stuck before the Desert, a Leviathan is the single biggest income jump available.

name: Camel
notes__en:
The Camel is the Desert's Rare, and for many players it is the first pet from the third biome. The Desert asks for a big jump in Speed compared with the Lake, so a Camel is a sign that your run is going well.

Camels have one of the heaviest base weights of any early pet. Because the base is already so heavy, a Camel that looks huge on its card is usually close to average, and its weight bonus is small.

Income-wise the Camel only beats the Lake's Turtle by a little, so the real reason to collect Camel eggs is the Speed reward, which is far higher than anything in the Lake. Use Camels to push toward the Jungle and Snow, and replace them with Epics as soon as you can.

name: Scorpion
notes__en:
The Scorpion is the Desert's guardian and also one of its best pets. It is a Mythic, a rarity above the Legendaries most players own when they first reach the Desert.

Stealing a Scorpion egg means going right up to the guardian, so bring Speed to spare. The egg hatches in about the same time as a Forest or Lake Legendary, which is short for a Mythic.

Its base income is several times the Desert's Legendary, the Snake, and its light base weight means a heavy Scorpion gets a strong weight bonus. The wiki infobox for this egg lists no reward, so the reward line is missing on this page.

name: Royal Sphinx
notes__en:
The Royal Sphinx is the Desert's Cosmic and the best pet in the third biome. It earns a bit more than the Lake's Leviathan and much more than the Desert's Mythics.

Its egg takes about half an hour to hatch, and its Speed reward is the highest of any Desert egg. The base weight is heavy, so a big kg number is normal.

If you have to choose between farming Scorpions or waiting on a Royal Sphinx, the Sphinx pays more over time, while Scorpions give a faster return.

The Tiger is the Jungle's guardian and its Mythic. The Jungle is the fourth biome, and the Tiger is the pet most players remember from it.

It earns more than the Desert's Scorpion, and its egg takes only a few minutes to hatch, so it is a quick upgrade once you can reach the Jungle and survive the run back.

Its base weight is moderate. The Speed reward on its egg is bigger than anything in the Desert except the Royal Sphinx, which makes Tiger eggs a good way to save up for Snow.

name: Walrus
notes__en:
The Walrus is the Snow biome's Epic. Snow needs a big jump in Speed over the Desert, so the Walrus is usually a mid-game pet.

It earns almost twice what a Swan does and its egg hatches faster than most Epics, which makes it a quick earner once you can reach Snow. Its base weight is high, so weight bonuses are smaller than on a light pet.

The Speed reward on a Walrus egg is several times the Lake's, which is the main reason to farm them. If you are saving for the next biome, a cycle of Walrus eggs works well, and the Polar Bear from the same biome is your next income goal.

name: Polar Bear
notes__en:
The Polar Bear is the Snow biome's Legendary. It earns more than twice what the Lake's Axolotl does, and its egg is the joint fastest Legendary egg in our list, hatching in less than half the Axolotl's time.

That short hatch time makes the Polar Bear a strong pick: you can hatch several while a slower Legendary egg would still be waiting. Its base weight is high, so weight bonuses are modest.

Reaching Snow needs a lot of Speed, so the Polar Bear marks the start of the mid game. Mythics from the same biome, such as the Sabertooth Tiger and Mammoth, are the next step up.

name: Yeti
notes__en:
The Yeti is the Snow biome's guardian and a Secret pet. Secret pets are a rarity above Cosmic, and the Yeti earns many times what the Snow's King Mammoth does.

Its egg is a commitment: it takes well over an hour and a half to hatch. Put it in your pen before you log off or go farm elsewhere.

The base weight is heavy. A Yeti is a long-term pet for a mid-game base, and only the Snow's Eternal, the Ice Dragon, beats it in the same biome.

name: Ice Dragon
notes__en:
The Ice Dragon is the Snow biome's Eternal pet, a rarity above Secret. It earns more than ten times what the Yeti from the same biome does.

That power comes with the longest wait of any Snow egg: about four hours to hatch. It makes sense to start one before a long break.

Players who can reach Snow but not much further often aim for the Ice Dragon as their top pet. Its base weight is heavy, so weight bonuses are small.

name: Cerberus
notes__en:
Cerberus is the Volcano's guardian and a Secret pet. It earns more than the Snow's Yeti, which makes it the strongest Secret most players see before the Abyss Ocean.

Its egg takes about two hours to hatch. Its base weight is very heavy, so expect very large kg numbers on its card.

The Volcano's Eternal pets, the Phoenix and Lava Dragon, earn more, but their eggs take far longer. A Cerberus is a strong pet to aim for while you build up Speed for the Abyss Ocean.

name: Phoenix
notes__en:
The Phoenix is one of the Volcano's Eternal pets. It earns more than the Snow's Ice Dragon and a little less than the Volcano's Lava Dragon.

Its base weight is light for an Eternal, much lighter than the Lava Dragon's. That makes a heavy Phoenix especially valuable, because weight bonuses are measured against the pet's own base.

Its egg takes about four and a half hours to hatch. For a player who can reach the Volcano, it is one of the best long-term pets in the biome.

name: Lava Dragon
notes__en:
The Lava Dragon is the best pet of the Volcano. It earns a little more than the Phoenix, the zone's other Eternal, and about twelve times what the Volcano's Secret, the Cerberus, makes.

Its egg is a five-hour hatch, slightly longer than the Phoenix egg, so if you can only fit in one long hatch, the Lava Dragon gives you the most for it. The community wiki lists a large Cash reward for the egg, one hundred times the pet's base income, which matches the pattern of most biome eggs.

Its base weight is heavy, far heavier than the Phoenix's. Keep that in mind when you compare two rolls by kilograms: the bonus depends on weight relative to the pet's own base.

The Shark is the Abyss Ocean's Legendary and the pet our calculator opens with. The Abyss Ocean is the seventh biome and needs a lot of Speed, so a Shark is a sign of a strong mid-game run.

It earns about twice what a Polar Bear does. Its egg gives a much larger Speed reward than any Snow egg, which helps you push toward the Prehistoric biome.

The Abyss Ocean is also where Dr. Scramble's cave is hidden, home of the shop that sells the Scrambled mutation consumable. Try a Shark with Golden or Rainbow in the calculator to see how much a mutation adds at this level.

notes__en:
The Kraken is the Abyss Ocean's Secret pet. It earns about twice what Cerberus does, so it is a clear upgrade once you can reach the seventh biome.

Its egg takes more than two hours to hatch and has a big Speed reward, which helps toward the Prehistoric biome.

Its base weight is very heavy, so a big kg number is normal. The Abyss Ocean's Eternal, El Maja, earns far more, but its egg takes even longer.

name: El Maja
notes__en:
El Maja is the Abyss Ocean's Eternal and the best pet you can hatch in that zone. It earns more than both Volcano Eternals and close to nine times as much as the Kraken, the Abyss Ocean's Secret.

Its egg takes about five and a half hours to hatch. That is a long wait, but the gap to the next pet in the zone is so large that it is worth planning around.

Its base weight is very heavy for an ocean pet. The next zone, Prehistoric, needs a big step up in Speed, so an El Maja is often the pet that carries a base through that grind.

Its egg takes about two and a half hours to hatch, and the Speed reward listed for it is far larger than any Abyss Ocean egg's.

Reaching the Prehistoric biome needs a huge amount of Speed, so a T-Rex is a late-game goal. The Mosasaurus from the same biome is an Eternal and earns several times more.

The Mosasaurus is the Eternal of the Prehistoric zone and the strongest pet there. It earns more than five times what the Tralaledon, the zone's best Secret, makes, and more than the Abyss Ocean's El Maja.

Its egg is a six-hour hatch, the longest in Prehistoric. The zone after this one, Cosmic, asks for a huge jump in Speed, so many players spend a long time here, and a few Mosasaurus pets are the usual goal for that stretch.

Prehistoric also has two Secrets, the Tralaledon and the T-Rex. They hatch faster, so they are a fair choice while you wait, but neither comes close to the Mosasaurus on income.

notes__en:
The Unicorn is the Divine of the Cosmic zone. Going through the zones in order, it is the first Divine you can hatch from a zone egg, which is why it is a milestone pet for many players.

It earns four times as much as the Eternal Lunar Dragon from the same zone. The catch is a twelve-hour hatch, so most players start a Unicorn egg before a long break rather than during play.

Its base weight is light for a Divine. Later zones have stronger Divines, the Kitsune first, but until you have the Speed for Cherry Blossom the Unicorn is the best pet you can work toward.

notes__en:
The Kitsune is the Divine of Cherry Blossom. It earns almost twice as much as the Cosmic zone's Unicorn and three times the Oni Tiger, the Eternal from its own zone.

Like the Unicorn, its egg needs twelve hours in the pen. Cherry Blossom asks for much less Speed than Titan Temple or Angels & Demons, so the Kitsune is a top-tier pet you can reach earlier than the other late Divines.

It has the lightest base weight of any Divine with a known weight in our list. Because weight bonuses are measured against the pet's own base, a Kitsune only needs to be a little heavier than its base to earn noticeably more.

tier_rationale__en: Ties with World Burner for the next spot; a Divine from Angels & Demons.
tier_rationale__id: Seri dengan World Burner untuk posisi berikutnya; pet Divine dari Angels & Demons.
notes__en:
ArchAngel is one of three Divine pets in Angels & Demons. Its base income is exactly the same as World Burner's, and the Aetheron from the same zone earns a bit more than both.

The ArchAngel egg needs eighteen hours to hatch, so think of it as an overnight egg. Its base weight is very heavy, one of the heaviest in our whole list, which means a heavy roll needs a lot of extra kilograms before the weight bonus shows.

Because the three Divines here hatch in the same time, the order to grab them is simple: Aetheron first, then ArchAngel or World Burner, whichever spawns near you.

name: World Burner
tier_rationale__en: Same base income as ArchAngel and spawns in the same zone, so take whichever egg you find first.

notes__en:
World Burner is one of the three Divine pets of Angels & Demons. On income it is a twin of ArchAngel: same base Cash per second, same base weight and the same eighteen-hour hatch, so neither is better than the other.

Inside its zone it sits behind the Aetheron only. Compared with the zone's Eternals it is a big jump, earning about three times what an Equinox makes and nearly four times a Pegasus.

Reaching Angels & Demons needs a lot of Speed, more than any zone except the Enchanted Forest. If you have just unlocked it, a World Burner egg is a strong first target, and you can swap it out later only for an Aetheron or a Spirit World Guardian.

name: Aetheron
tier_rationale__en: Best earner in Angels & Demons and second overall among pets that are still obtainable.
tier_rationale__id: Penghasil terbaik di Angels & Demons dan nomor dua dari semua pet yang masih bisa didapat.
notes__en:
The Aetheron is the top earner of Angels & Demons. It beats the zone's other two Divines, ArchAngel and World Burner, by about two fifths, and all three eggs take the same eighteen hours to hatch, so when you have the choice the Aetheron egg is the one to carry home.

It is also far lighter than those two, about a tenth of their base weight. Weight bonuses are measured against each pet's own base, so a few extra kilograms already count for more on an Aetheron.

If you want Speed rather than Cash, look at the zone's Pegasus and Skeleton Horse eggs instead: the community wiki lists the biggest Speed reward of any egg for them. The Aetheron is the pick once you just want income.
source_note: Base income and weight from the wiki pet data module

notes__en:
Grave Cerberus is a Secret pet that hatches from the Halloween Egg in the Halloween Dimension. Don't mix it up with the Volcano's Cerberus: on the wiki's numbers the Grave version earns dozens of times more, so it is a big jump for anyone still running Volcano pets.
It is not the best Secret of the event, though. Werewolf, from the same zone, earns roughly three times as much. The wiki lists a very short hatch time for the Halloween Egg, which makes Grave Cerberus a quick early target when you first reach the event zone, before you chase the rarer eggs.

name: Spirit World Guardian
tier_rationale__en: Highest base income of any pet you can hatch right now. Its egg spawns in the Enchanted Forest, the newest and farthest zone.
tier_rationale__id: Pendapatan dasar tertinggi dari semua pet yang bisa kamu tetaskan sekarang. Telurnya muncul di Enchanted Forest, zona terbaru dan paling jauh.
notes__en:
The Spirit World Guardian is the Divine pet of the Enchanted Forest, the newest zone in Steal an Egg. No pet that spawns in a zone earns more in our list: it makes almost four times as much as the Aetheron, the best pet of Angels & Demons.

Getting one is slow. The Enchanted Forest asks for two and a half times the Speed of Angels & Demons, and the egg needs about twenty hours in your pen, the longest hatch of any egg we list. Start it before you log off for the night.

The rest of the zone is a long way behind. The next best Enchanted Forest pet, the Spirit Panda, earns well under one percent as much, so for most players this zone is about one egg only.

name: Voidseer Pumpkin
notes__en:
The Voidseer Pumpkin is the Divine pet of the Halloween Dimension, the event zone of the Halloween event. On the community wiki's numbers it is the second-best earner in the whole game, behind only the Enchanted Forest's Spirit World Guardian, and it earns more than three times what the Abomination Kong, the best Eternal in the same zone, makes.
It hatches only from its own egg, the Voidseer Pumpkin Egg, which you have to carry out of the Halloween Dimension. Event pets are marked limited here: when the event zone closes, the egg will most likely stop appearing, so a Voidseer Pumpkin you already own is worth keeping rather than trading away cheap.
